items.title: 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. “Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. He said INEC considered introducing a new electoral technology for 2027 but chose to upgrade its existing infrastructure because of the tight timeline before the polls. To address the malfunctions of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) linked to heat and storage conditions in 2023, he said INEC was building climate-controlled storage facilities in all states. The commission has also bought extra devices and cut the maximum number of voters assigned per BVAS from 1,250 to 850, so that polling units with more than 850 registered voters will get multiple devices. On funding, Amupitan said INEC had received a substantial part of its 2027 election budget and had been assured that the outstanding balance, part of which is meant for the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc staff, would be released before the end of November. Responding to allegations on social media that linked his phone number to a controversial X account, he denied ever operating one. He said an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation. He dismissed suggestions that his past legal representation in political disputes would affect his impartiality. “My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he said. On claims of an 85 per cent surge in registrants in a ward in Ebonyi State, he said the commission had investigated and resolved the complaint in line with statutory procedures. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on February 6, 2027. Amupitan urged young Nigerians to stay involved in the democratic process. “Misinformation remains one of the greatest threats to our democracy. Citizens must verify information before acting or sharing, and give our democracy the chance to succeed,” he said. The post 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fiasco Lyhanna : Darmanin saisit le CSM, après les multiples manquements d’une magistrate
items.description: Selon Le Figaro et Le Parisien , le garde des Sceaux Gerald Darmanin vient de saisir le Conseil superieur de la magistrature (CSM). Une saisine, qui fait suite aux investigations de l'Inspection generale judiciaire (IGJ) dans l'affaire Lyhanna, en vue d'eventuelles poursuites a l'encontre d'une substitute du parquet d'Auch. « C'est a la lumiere de la remise du troisieme rapport sur le fonctionnement du parquet d'Auch et de l'enquete administrative visant une substitute de ce meme parquet que le ministre de la Justice a pris sa decision de poursuivre la magistrate devant la formation parquet du CSM », a relate Le Figaro , precisant que cette magistrate n'a pour l'heure pas « pu etre entendue pour des raisons medicales ». Celle-ci n'aurait, a liste Le Parisien , pas fixe de delai a l'enquete concernant une plainte de la petite Rosa – une precedente victime de Jerome Barella qui, selon les inspecteurs, a ete violee « une cinquantaine de fois » – deposee en août 2025, soit dix mois avant l'enlevement, le viol et le meurtre de Lyhanna. Elle n'aurait pas non plus verifie les antecedents judiciaires de Jerome Barella, ni saisi le bon service d'enquete. Ou plutot, a en croire les elements des enquetes administratives rapportes par Le Parisien , elle n'aurait pas verifie le soit-transmis « prepare et prerempli par une assistante de justice », qu'elle aurait alors signe « sans le completer, ni le corriger ». « De quoi se demander si elle l'a meme lu », a ajoute le quotidien concernant cette magistrate « installee comme substitut du procureur […] sans passer le stage pratique, une courte formation obligatoire » et qui avait quelques mois plus tot « arrete quatre mois […] pour epuisement professionnel ». Le 4 juin, apres plusieurs jours de recherche, le corps sans vie de Lyhanna, jeune adolescente de 11 ans, disparue a la sortie de son college de Fleurance, dans le Gers, avait ete retrouve dans un silo agricole desaffecte. Lors de l'autopsie, un viol est constate et l'ADN du principal suspect, Jerome Barella, est retrouve sur le corps de la fillette. Avant meme cette macabre decouverte, les regards s'etaient tournes vers cet homme, ayant fait l'objet de multiples signalements et plaintes pour attouchement sur mineurs. Des plaintes a la suite desquels le mis en cause n'avait pas ete inquiete. Ces revelations avaient provoque une deflagration mediatique et populaire en France. Comme le precisent les deux medias, c'est dorenavant au CSM qu'il revient de statuer sur ces manquements releves, et de dire s'ils constituent des fautes disciplinaires.

items.title: Imran's key message from jail is to 'stick firmly to the ideology': PTI secretary general
items.description: Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan wants his party leaders to “stick firmly to the ideology” of the party, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Thursday. Following the Islamabad High Court’s order to jail authorities to facilitate meetings for legal consultation, lawyers Barrister Salman Safdar and Advocate Latif Khosa were able to meet Imran and his wife , Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail on Wednesday. According to both lawyers, the meeting lasted at least three hours and mainly focused on the couple’s legal and health issues. However, they did not divulge further details; the government often objects to lawyers using such meetings to make political statements. Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’ on Thursday, Raja said that he had multiple detailed conversations with Barrister Safdar following the latter’s meeting with Imran. “Imran Khan’s fundamental message was to stick firmly to the ideology,” the PTI secretary general said, conveying details he heard from Safdar. “I have also been directed to stick to [our] ideology,” Raja added, noting that Imran’s “fundamental message is not to bow”. He further said Imran reiterated his support for National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, whom the PTI founder had picked for their respective roles. He quoted Imran as saying that Achakzai and Abbas were not individuals who would “bow down or be sold”, and he had nominated them after deep contemplation. “Imran Khan sahib ’s directives will be acted upon,” the PTI secretary general declared. He added that Imran had also issued instructions on the issue of the formation of new provinces during his meetings with Safdar, including the one on Nov 2 . “Imran Khan is not ready to step back from his ideology of democracy and public welfare […] the rule of the people is the foremost priority of Imran Khan,” Raja stated. He said that Imran considered concerns related to his well-being as unnecessary; however, the party was concerned about his health, as Imran’s blood pressure was not stable. Raja claimed that Imran had also reported in yesterday’s meeting about his blood pressure “reaching 193 on Saturday”. Asked whether this message could be considered political and thereby hinder chances of future jail meetings, Raja contended that although a handful of matters were discussed during the three-hour-long huddle, everything was monitored and recorded via microphones. He noted that Khosa, who was also an MNA, has made several statements after the meeting, which “compelled Safdar to clarify matters”. Regarding himself, the PTI secretary general said Imran had issued instructions to him regarding standing with the principles and reorganisation of the party. He acknowledged that there was a small faction in the PTI which is displeased with him. However, he emphasised that Imran’s directives conveyed to him were different. “Imran Khan’s message for me is to create space while upholding the principles and move forward,” Raja said, denying other notions coming from different circles within the PTI. Regarding directives issued by Imran on a possible 28th constitutional amendment, the PTI secretary general said he would put this matter before the party leadership first. The directions were related to standing with democratic principles and the rights of small provinces, he said, adding that the PTI founder had always supported the creation of new administrative units. However, Raja noted that there had been some concerns related to the “context” behind the formation of new administrative units and stressed the importance of the public’s opinion. Imran’s meeting not linked to 28th amendment: Sanaullah Meanwhile, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah denied speculation that Imran’s meeting with his lawyers was linked to the process of introducing a 28th constitutional amendment. “This was just a simple meeting between lawyers who agreed to present an argument in court and enable it to decide on an appeal,” he told Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada ke Saath’, noting that people have been trying to link the meeting to the 28th amendment or other matters. The PM’s aide explained that Safdar and Khosa did not present their arguments before the IHC, contending that they could not do so without meeting their clients. “The IHC chief justice said that if they promised to argue the case, he would arrange a meeting. As a result of the commitment, the meeting was permitted and both of them were able to meet [Imran and Bushra],” Sanaullah said. “This political theory that the meeting was held to discuss the 28th Amendment is completely incorrect; there is no such thing,” the PML-N leader maintained. He was then asked about the government’s knowledge of the matter, considering the lengthy meeting allowed Imran to discuss political issues with his lawyers. In response, Sanaullah said officials of the interior ministry were aware of the meeting as it was their domain. Asked whether there was any “distance” emerging between the government and the “institutions”, the PML-N leader replied, “Distancing from us can never begin, and neither will it. “There is exemplary coordination between the military and civilian leadership,” he affirmed. Highlighting Pakistan’s achievements in the diplomatic and military arena, he said: “This situation should remain, and everyone should pray that this situation remains forever.”

items.title: Médecine traditionnelle au Sénégal : vers un cadre juridique mieux adapté
items.description: Mettre en place un cadre juridique adapté pour mieux organiser la médecine traditionnelle au Sénégal, reconnaître les praticiens, valoriser les savoirs endogènes et garantir la protection des populations, c’est ce que vise le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique. Le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique a organisé une rencontre de trois jours réunissant chercheurs, juristes, tradipraticiens et partenaires techniques et financiers, en vue de finaliser un avant-projet de loi sur la médecine traditionnelle, complémentaire et intégrative pour la santé (MTCIS). « Cette initiative vise à mettre en place un cadre juridique adapté pour mieux organiser le secteur, reconnaître les praticiens, valoriser les savoirs endogènes et garantir la protection des populations », renseigne la tutelle dans une note publiée jeudi. A lire aussi : Lutte contre les médicaments frauduleux: une semaine pour sensibiliser Malgré les avancées enregistrées dans la réglementation des médicaments à base de plantes, poursuit le texte, plusieurs aspects restent à encadrer, notamment les pratiques des tradipraticiens, la recherche, l’intégration aux soins de santé primaires et la préservation de la biodiversité. Pour le Dr Mor Diagne, conseiller technique du ministre chargé de la Pharmacie, l’enjeu est de « protéger à la fois les patients, les praticiens et les écosystèmes ». Ainsi, les travaux ont permis de formuler des propositions concrètes qui seront compilées dans un document de référence pour la poursuite du processus d’élaboration de l’avant-projet de loi, avant sa soumission à l’Assemblée nationale. Mariama DIEME

items.title: 11 killed, 2 injured as passenger van plunges into river in GB's Ghizer: police
items.description: GILGIT: Eleven people were killed and two injured when a passenger vehicle plunged into a river in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Ghizer district on Thursday. According to local police, a passenger van was en route to Ghizer’s Yasin Valley from Gilgit on Thursday evening when the driver lost control near Morkah Bridge, causing the van to plunge into the Yasin river. Police initially said rescue teams retrieved the bodies of 10 passengers, including two women. They also rescued three injured passengers, including a child, who were taken to the Gupis Civil Hospital for treatment. In an update, police said the death toll had risen to 11, including an infant, while two were injured. Police said the deceased and injured were residents of Yasin Valley, adding that an investigation was under way to identify the cause of the incident. GB Chief Minister Amjad Hussain expressed deep grief and sorrow over the loss of lives in the accident. He directed the district administration, rescue agencies, and relevant health department officials to ensure the injured were immediately transported to nearby hospitals and to utilise all available resources to provide the best possible medical facilities. He also instructed the administration to ensure that no negligence occurred during rescue operations, and that the medical treatment and care of the injured were carefully monitored. Expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families, Hussain said the loss of human lives in the tragic accident was “deeply distressing”. He prayed for eternal peace for the deceased and strength to their families to bear the loss, while hoping for the speedy recovery of the injured. Three people were killed and 13 others injured in a collision between a coach and a motorcycle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan on Wednesday, according to Rescue 1122. Last week, eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus travelling from Gilgit to Islamabad collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway. The day before, a collision between a passenger bus and a truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Punjab’s Pakpattan.

items.title: CRIEF : AGETIPE, Phamagui, comptes gelés… Wright fait le point sur les dossiers sensibles
items.description: Le procureur spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), Charles Wright, était l’invité de l’émission « Guinée Today » sur Télé 24, ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026. Au cours de cet entretien, il est revenu sur plusieurs dossiers judiciaires sensibles, notamment celui de l’AGETIPE, les procédures visant certains anciens responsables publics ainsi que les présumées irrégularités dans la gestion de la Pharmacie centrale de Guinée (PHARMAGUI). Le magistrat a également défendu sa démarche, fondée, selon lui, sur la rigueur des enquêtes, la recherche des preuves et la lutte contre l’enrichissement illicite. Interrogé sur le bilan de son prédécesseur, Aly Touré, le procureur spécial a reconnu les difficultés auxquelles celui-ci a été confronté, tout en saluant les efforts accomplis à la tête du parquet spécial. Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, le bilan d'un responsable judiciaire doit être apprécié à travers les actes posés et les résultats obtenus, plutôt que sur la base d'une recherche d'unanimité. Abordant sa propre méthode de travail, il a révélé qu'à son arrivée à la CRIEF, il avait constaté qu'environ 19 à 20 dossiers avaient été communiqués aux fins d'instruction au cours de l'année précédente. En trois jours, a-t-il expliqué, il a saisi la chambre compétente dans le cadre de 25 procédures, après avoir constaté que plusieurs rapports étaient restés sans orientation judiciaire. Le procureur spécial a toutefois tenu à rappeler qu'une enquête financière ne peut être conduite dans la précipitation. Selon lui, les investigations nécessitent du temps pour établir les responsabilités, vérifier les mouvements financiers et réunir des éléments susceptibles de soutenir les poursuites. Dossier AGETIPE : le parquet privilégie une enquête approfondie Sur la question de l'enquête visant le directeur général de l'Agence Guinéenne d’Execution Des Travaux D’intérêt Public pour l’Emploi (AGETIPE), Charles Wright a expliqué que les investigations doivent tenir compte de l'ensemble de la période concernée par les faits signalés. Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas limiter les vérifications au seul responsable actuellement en fonction. Pour lui, lorsqu'il s'agit de la gestion des ressources publiques, il faut également examiner les responsabilités des anciens dirigeants et retracer les décisions prises successivement. Le magistrat estime qu'un responsable ne saurait être automatiquement tenu pour responsable de toutes les irrégularités constatées durant son mandat sans que les circonstances de chaque dépense soient examinées. Il a ainsi défendu une approche au cas par cas, afin de déterminer les responsabilités réelles et d'éviter les accusations injustifiées. Biens présumés illicites : Wright insiste sur la traçabilité des fortunes Autre point important de son intervention : la question de l'enrichissement des anciens responsables publics. Le procureur spécial a évoqué des situations dans lesquelles des montants considérables sont retrouvés sur des comptes bancaires, tout en soulignant qu'il appartient aux investigations de déterminer si ces sommes proviennent ou non d'activités délictueuses. Il a notamment rappelé que la présence de plusieurs milliards de francs guinéens sur un compte bancaire ne suffit pas, à elle seule, à établir l'existence d'une infraction. L'origine des fonds doit être vérifiée et confrontée aux éléments de l'enquête. Dans cette perspective, il a défendu les mesures conservatoires, notamment le gel de certains comptes, comme des instruments permettant de préserver les intérêts de l'État pendant les procédures judiciaires. Alphonse Charles Wright a également affirmé que la politique de redevabilité doit désormais s'imposer à tous les responsables publics, indépendamment de leur rang ou de leur proximité avec les autorités. Interdictions de sortie du territoire : les cadres concernés invités à répondre aux enquêteurs Sur les restrictions de déplacement visant certains responsables, le procureur spécial a justifié le maintien des interdictions de sortie du territoire par la nécessité de garantir la disponibilité des personnes concernées devant les enquêteurs. Il a expliqué que plusieurs personnes ayant fait l'objet de procédures judiciaires avaient quitté le pays sans répondre aux convocations de la justice. Pour éviter que de telles situations ne se reproduisent, il estime nécessaire de prendre des précautions. Il a toutefois précisé que les personnes concernées peuvent se rapprocher des enquêteurs, donner leur version des faits et présenter leurs moyens de défense avant d'envisager un déplacement à l'étranger. Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, ces mesures ne doivent pas être interprétées comme une condamnation anticipée, mais comme des dispositions liées aux nécessités de l'enquête. Pharmacie centrale de Guinée : de présumées pratiques irrégulières dans les marchés publics dénoncées L'un des passages les plus marquants de l'émission a concerné la gestion de la Pharmacie centrale de Guinée et les procédures visant son directeur général, le Dr Labilé Sagno, ainsi que plusieurs autres cadres. Sans se présenter comme un spécialiste du domaine pharmaceutique, Alphonse Charles Wright a dénoncé plusieurs pratiques qu'il estime particulièrement préoccupantes dans la gestion des achats de médicaments. Il a notamment évoqué de possibles conflits d'intérêts, faisant état de responsables qui auraient orienté des commandes vers des officines leur appartenant ou créées par leurs soins. Le procureur spécial a également soulevé la question de l'acquisition de médicaments dont les dates de péremption seraient proches. Selon ses explications, certaines pratiques pourraient consister à gonfler les montants des marchés tout en privilégiant des produits dont la valeur commerciale diminue à mesure que leur date d'expiration approche. Ces déclarations mettent en lumière les enjeux liés à la transparence dans les marchés publics et à la protection de la santé des populations. Dans un pays où l'accès aux médicaments demeure une préoccupation majeure, le fonctionnement de la centrale d'approvisionnement revêt une importance particulière. « Où sont les preuves ? » : le procureur appelle à des dénonciations documentées Dans un autre registre, Alphonse Charles Wright a lancé un appel aux citoyens qui dénoncent des faits présumés de corruption ou de détournement de deniers publics. Il les a invités à accompagner leurs accusations de documents et d'éléments vérifiables. « Toi qui dénonces, où sont les pièces ? Envoie-moi les preuves de ce que tu dénonces », a-t-il insisté. Le procureur spécial a ainsi expliqué qu'il ne souhaitait pas engager des procédures sur la seule base de rumeurs, de publications sur les réseaux sociaux ou d'informations non vérifiées. Pour lui, toute dénonciation doit reposer sur des éléments suffisamment sérieux pour justifier l'ouverture d'investigations. « La plus grande prison, c'est la conscience » Au-delà des dossiers judiciaires, Wright a livré un plaidoyer en faveur de la responsabilité des cadres de l'administration publique. Il estime que l'accès à une fonction de responsabilité doit être considéré comme un engagement au service de la nation et non comme une occasion d'enrichissement personnel. Il a également reconnu les pressions et les difficultés auxquelles peuvent être confrontés les magistrats chargés de poursuivre des personnalités influentes. Malgré les critiques et les attaques, il affirme vouloir poursuivre son travail, estimant que la lutte contre la corruption constitue un impératif pour l'avenir du pays. A travers cette intervention sur Télé24, le procureur spécial de la CRIEF a voulu réaffirmer sa détermination à poursuivre les investigations sur les présumées infractions économiques et financières. Un message qui intervient dans un contexte où les attentes des Guinéens restent fortes quant à la transparence dans la gestion des ressources publiques et à l'aboutissement des procédures judiciaires.

items.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027 : le Syli national domine l’Érythrée et consolide sa deuxième place
items.description: Le Syli national de Guinée s'est imposé ce jeudi 12 novembre face à l’Érythrée (2-1), au stade du 28 Septembre, à l’occasion de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2027. Un succès qui permet aux hommes de Paulo Duarte de consolider leur deuxième place dans le groupe D avec six points. Les Guinéens n’ont pas tardé à prendre les devants dans cette rencontre. Dès la 13e minute de jeu, Mohamed Soumah a ouvert le score de la tête, à la suite d’un corner, donnant ainsi l’avantage au Syli national. Malgré quelques tentatives de part et d’autre, le score est resté inchangé jusqu’à la pause. Au retour des vestiaires, le sélectionneur guinéen Paulo Duarte a décidé de réajuster son dispositif avec trois changements. Thierno Barry, Ousmane Camara et Gnagna Barry ont ainsi fait leur entrée en jeu. Un coaching rapidement récompensé puisque, dès la 53e minute, Gnagna Barry, attaquant du Horoya AC, a inscrit le deuxième but guinéen. Alors que la Guinée semblait se diriger vers une victoire tranquille, l’Érythrée a relancé le suspense en fin de rencontre. À la 83e minute, Ismail Maill Lundgreen a réduit l’écart, redonnant espoir à son équipe. Mais le Syli national a su préserver son avantage jusqu’au coup de sifflet final et s’imposer sur le score de 2 buts à 1. Grâce à cette victoire, la Guinée totalise désormais six points et conserve sa deuxième place au classement du groupe D, derrière l’Afrique du Sud, qui doit affronter le Kenya ce vendredi. Les hommes de Paulo Duarte auront toutefois peu de temps pour savourer ce succès. Ils retrouveront l’Érythrée le 16 novembre prochain au Caire, en Égypte, pour le compte de la quatrième journée de ces éliminatoires. Une nouvelle occasion pour le Syli national de confirmer sa dynamique et de conforter ses ambitions de qualification pour la CAN 2027. Sadjo Bah L’article Éliminatoires CAN 2027 : le Syli national domine l’Érythrée et consolide sa deuxième place est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Élim.CAN2027 : sans Guirassy, le Syli domine l’Érythrée et se relance dans la course à la qualification
items.description: La Guinée a battu l’Érythrée (2-1), ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, au stade du 28-Septembre de Conakry, à l’occasion de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2027. Malgré une préparation perturbée et plusieurs absences de taille, le Syli National a assuré l’essentiel devant son public et relance ainsi ses chances de qualification. Dès le coup d’envoi, les hommes de Paulo Duarte ont pris les commandes de la rencontre, portés par un public venu nombreux au stade du 28-Septembre. Les Guinéens n’ont pas tardé à concrétiser leur domination. À la 12e minute, le défenseur central Mohamed Soumah, monté aux avant-postes à la faveur d’un corner, a ouvert le score et permis au Syli de prendre l’avantage. Après ce but, les Érythréens ont tenté de revenir dans la partie en multipliant les offensives. Leurs incursions ont notamment mis à contribution le gardien guinéen, Mohamed Richard Camara, auteur d’une double parade spectaculaire qui a permis à son équipe de conserver son avance. À l’autre bout du terrain, Kerfala Cissoko, titularisé à la pointe de l’attaque en l’absence de Serhou Guirassy, a eu l’occasion de faire le break. Bien servi dans la surface, l’attaquant a toutefois complètement manqué sa frappe, expédiant le ballon au-dessus de la cage adverse. Au retour des vestiaires, le sélectionneur portugais Paulo Duarte a effectué trois changements. Un coaching rapidement récompensé puisque Yaghouba Gnagna Barry, fraîchement entré en jeu, a inscrit le deuxième but guinéen à la 52e minute. Menés de deux buts, les visiteurs n’ont cependant pas abdiqué. À la 82e minute, Ismail Mail a réduit le score d’une frappe qui n’a laissé aucune chance au portier guinéen. Mohamed Richard Camara, pourtant décisif à plusieurs reprises depuis le début de la rencontre, n’a cette fois-ci rien pu faire. Les dernières minutes ont alors pris des allures de suspense pour le Syli National. Acculés par les offensives érythréennes, les Guinéens ont progressivement reculé, laissant planer la menace d’une égalisation. Mais, malgré cette fin de rencontre sous pression, la défense guinéenne a résisté jusqu’au coup de sifflet final. Avec cette victoire (2-1), la Guinée engrange trois précieux points et se relance dans la course à la qualification pour la CAN 2027. Le Syli devra désormais attendre l’issue de l'autre rencontre du groupe D entre l’Afrique du Sud et le Kenya pour connaître les éventuelles répercussions de ce succès sur le classement.

items.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
items.description: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat. Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager. Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”. “A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football. Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended. Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey. He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16. Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history. Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024. He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi. “What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain. items.title: Man United closing in on Pochettino after sacking manager Carrick
items.description: United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to be appointed as the new manager of Manchester United after the struggling English giants sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday. Pochettino is expected to leave his role with the USA following their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday and Tuesday in a move that will see United trigger a release clause worth some $10 million to secure the Argentine’s services. Pochettino, who signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago, is due to hold a pre-match press conference on Friday. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish in the Premier League last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement Thursday that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions,” United said. “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.” Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club’s hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away despite a paltry record of three wins from 15 games in all competitions this season. It is believed Carrick’s future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. – ‘Disgusting’ – Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013. Former United captain Gary Neville, who played alongside Carrick, said his old team-mate had been treated appallingly. “It’s just quite simply disgusting,” Neville told Sky Sports. “That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business. In any other industry it would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.” The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust said Carrick’s departure marked “another depressing moment”, pinning the blame on majority owners the Glazer family and minority shareholder Ratcliffe, with the club yet to win a Premier League title since the end of the Ferguson era. “The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club,” MUST said in a statement. “When (Ratcliffe’s) INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.” United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. items.title: ‎Nigeria has left ’emergency ward,’ targets $1trn economy by 2030 – Tinubu
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ President Bola Tinubu on Thursday declared that Nigeria’s economy has moved “from stabilisation to shared prosperity,” citing non-oil exports above $6 billion, external reserves of about $55 billion, and a target of a $1 trillion economy by 2030. ‎ ‎Speaking at the public presentation of Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: Past, Present and Future, authored by Honourable Abdulmumin Jibrin Kofa, Tinubu said the country had abandoned “cosmetic remedies” for what he called the “hard road of surgery.” ‎ ‎According to him: “For too long, Nigeria’s story was a song sung in a single note. We were a nation of boundless promise tied to a single product, our budget, our currency and the livelihoods of millions rising and falling with the tides of a distant oil market. We floated on the fragile illusion of oil wealth while the foundations beneath us crackborders. ‎ ‎”When I took the oath of office, I did not inherit a calm sea; I inherited a gathering storm: a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent as industries and jobs fled across our borders.” ‎ ‎The President said his administration inherited “a gathering storm,” including “a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent.” ‎ ‎“We chose reform over ruin. We removed the fuel subsidy. We unified the exchange rate. These were not easy decisions, and I know the weight they placed on every household. But they were necessary, and today the pain is yielding its promise.” ‎ ‎He stated that non-oil activities now account for about 96 per cent of Gross Domestic Product, while non-oil exports have crossed $6 billion, which he described as the highest in Nigeria’s history. ‎ ‎Tinubu also said external reserves had risen to about $55 billion, representing “more than fourteen months of import cover,” and that non-oil revenue had grown from ₦13.63 trillion in 2023 to ₦16.4 trillion in the first half of 2026. ‎ ‎The President said government alone cannot build a $1 trillion economy, adding that wealth must be created by enterprises that “invest, innovate, manufacture and export.” ‎ ‎“Our duty is to clear the path before them,” he said. “That is why our 2025 budget introduced a first-of-its-kind De-risking Framework to draw in private capital, which we expect to provide 86 per cent of the investment our 2030 goal demands.” ‎ ‎He said the administration was harmonising taxes and ending “the menace of multiple taxation.” ‎“We cannot tax our way into prosperity; we must produce our way there,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎The President said the administration had “fought for Mambilla,” winning a $3.38 billion arbitration at the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris and freeing “a project held hostage for more than nine years.” ‎He added that Geregu Power is moving to raise its capacity to 1,300 megawatts, while the Port Harcourt and Warri refineries are “stirring back to life.” ‎ ‎On infrastructure, Tinubu listed the Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway, Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano Expressway, East–West Road, Ibadan–Ife–Ilesa Expressway, Port Harcourt–Enugu and Enugu–Onitsha expressways, and the restoration of Carter Bridge. ‎ ‎He said 52 per cent of legacy highway mileage is in the North and 48 per cent in the South. ‎ ‎“We are building fairly and deliberately, so that no zone is left behind and no citizen is a stranger to opportunity,” he said. ‎ ‎Tinubu said more than 10,000 homes are rising across 14 states and the Federal Capital Territory under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. ‎He said the MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund had provided about ₦128 billion in mortgages to 1,859 families in 25 states, at a fixed rate of 9.75 per cent over 20 years. ‎ ‎“As this market grows, so must the confidence of those who invest in it,” he said. “I will therefore work hand in hand with the National Assembly and stakeholders to establish a strong regulatory authority for housing and real estate.” ‎ ‎The President also cited NELFUND, university solarisation, Bank of Industry loans and grants across all 774 local government areas, the 3MTT digital-skills programme, and 90,000 kilometres of fibre-optic infrastructure. ‎“Roads and power lines are the skeleton of a nation; its people are its life,” he said. ‎ ‎Tinubu commended Jibrin, the member representing Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency in Kano State, whose years as a lawmaker and chairman of key National Assembly committees, including Finance and Appropriations, “lend these pages the weight of experience.” ‎ ‎“This is the essence of the book we present today,” Tinubu said. “It looks back with honesty, looks around with clarity and looks ahead with courage.” ‎ ‎He said: “The days of hardship are temporary; the foundations we are laying are permanent. Let us keep building until the world looks upon Nigeria and sees not promise deferred, but promise fulfilled.” ‎ ‎The event was held at the State House Conference Centre in Abuja, with Governor Charles Soludo as keynote speaker, Alhaji Abdulsamad Isyaku Rabiu as book presenter and Dr Reuben Abati as reviewer. items.title: 2027: Tinubu will lose if he contests against anybody picked on street — Dalung
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Solomon Dalung has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would lose the 2027 election even if his opponent were “anybody picked on the street,” arguing that the President was afraid of facing voters. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Dalung made the prediction while responding to a question about how the opposition could overcome the APC’s resources amid the current internal leadership and legal crisis in the ADC. He nevertheless insisted the party was ready to challenge Tinubu at the ballot. “Since my experience in politics, like I always say, Nigerians, I was brought into politics at a much tender age. I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” Dalung said. He claimed Tinubu was apprehensive about the election despite having been in office for four years, and challenged the President and APC to let the contest be decided by voters. “Bola Tinubu is so scared, having been in office for four years, he is so scared of election. And all we are seeing in ADC, let’s meet at the ballot. You claim it was the ballot that brought you to power, let’s meet at the ballot,” he said. Dalung also accused the APC of obstructing opposition parties’ campaign activities, alleging that venues had been closed, hotels taken over and party offices sealed. He compared the situation with the 2014 election period, saying the APC would have been left with few places to campaign if it had faced similar restrictions then. “Nobody will be blamed except Tinubu. Why? Because I mean, in the history of Nigeria, we have seen opposition parties contest election, but we have never seen this type of situation. If the PDP in 2014 were closing venues for rallies and taking over hotels, sealing party offices, the APC would have no place to campaign except the streets,” he said. He argued that moving the opposition onto the streets would not weaken its campaign, claiming those attending its gatherings were genuine supporters rather than people hired to fill rallies. “Now, for Tinubu and his APC to move the opposition on pit, they have lost the election. This is because the people we are having on the street are organic followers. Those are the Nigerians that will vote. They are not rented crowds from all over the federation,” Dalung said. items.title: Reps condemn political violence as thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos; NDC, APC-PCC fault attack
items.description: By By Henry Umoru, and Gift ChapiOdekina The House of Representatives, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) have condemned reported cases of political violence across the country following an attack on NDC supporters during a town hall meeting in Lagos. While the NDC demanded an immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the attack in Lagos, the APC-PCC also condemned the incident and called on security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators. The Lagos State chapter of the APC equally condemned the reported attack but denied any involvement, challenging the NDC to provide credible evidence linking the ruling party to the incident. The House of Representatives, on Wednesday, also resolved to investigate reported attacks, intimidation and disruption of political activities across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers, amid growing concerns over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country. Presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies to maintain public peace. Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties. He also cited the constitutional provision which makes the security and welfare of the people the primary purpose of government, stressing the need to protect citizens participating in legitimate political activities. Agbedi urged the House to invoke Section 88(1) of the Constitution, which empowers the National Assembly to investigate matters within its legislative competence and examine the conduct of public authorities responsible for administering relevant laws. To illustrate the growing concerns, he cited several incidents of political violence recorded in different states. He recalled the disruption of political meetings in Enugu State on September 12, 2026, during which the police reportedly confirmed that two attendees were injured, while one person was allegedly killed. He also cited an attack on APC supporters travelling to a rally in Katsina State on October 28, 2026, which led to the arrest of 14 suspects. In Nasarawa State, Agbedi recalled the attack on an APC rally in Lafia on November 4, 2026, where several people were reportedly injured. He further mentioned a violent incident during a political procession in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7, 2026, in which the police reportedly confirmed that one person was killed and five others injured. The lawmaker warned that continued attacks, intimidation and destruction of property linked to political activities could result in further loss of lives and injuries, while discouraging citizens from participating in the electoral process. He, however, stressed that allegations of responsibility for the incidents must be established through impartial, thorough and evidence-based investigations. The House subsequently constituted an ad hoc committee headed by the Leader of the House, Julius Ihonvbere, to investigate the immediate and remote causes of politically motivated violence and report its findings within three weeks. The committee comprises the House Leader, Minority Leader, chairmen and deputy chairmen of the House Committees on Police Affairs and National Security and Intelligence, as well as two additional members drawn from the committees. NDC demands probe, prosecution Meanwhile, the national leadership of the NDC has condemned the attack on its supporters by suspected political thugs who allegedly invaded its town hall meeting in Oregun, along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos. The party demanded the immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible, insisting that the incident would not intimidate its members or silence Nigerians. In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the Spokesperson of the NDC National Campaign Council, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the party described the incident as an unacceptable assault on democracy, citizens’ fundamental rights and freedom of political association. It said no political party or group had a monopoly on Nigeria, adding that nobody had the right to deploy violence, intimidation or thuggery to silence opposing voices. The party also called for an end to what it described as the dangerous culture of political violence being witnessed in some states. The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) strongly condemns the violent attack on its supporters in Lagos by suspected political thugs during its town hall meeting today. “We deeply sympathise with anybody injured in the attack and wish them a speedy and full recovery. Our thoughts are with them and their families at this difficult time. “This incident is an unacceptable assault on democracy, citizens’ fundamental rights and the freedom of political association. No political party or group has a monopoly on Nigeria, and no one has the right to use violence, intimidation or thuggery to silence opposing voices. “Nigeria is not a conquered territory, and political participation is not a crime. “We demand an immediate investigation, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and an end to the dangerous culture of political violence we are witnessing in some states. “Those who believe they can intimidate Nigerians into silence must understand that democracy belongs to the people, not political thugs and their sponsors.” The party alleged that the attack was part of an attempt to intimidate Nigerians, spread fear and discourage participation in the 2027 elections, but insisted that such efforts would fail. The Lagos meeting was part of the NDC’s campaign activities in support of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and governorship candidate, Funsho Doherty. The party urged Nigerians to turn out in large numbers in 2027 to exercise their democratic rights and vote for the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket, describing the call as part of its demand for accountable leadership and a different direction for the country. It maintained that neither the party nor its supporters would be bullied out of exercising their democratic rights. APC-PCC calls for arrests Similarly, the APC Presidential Campaign Council condemned the disruption of the NDC town hall meeting in Lagos and other reported attacks on political gatherings in Edo, Cross River and Gombe states. In a statement issued on Thursday, the Spokesperson of the APC-PCC, Dele Alake, described the attacks as condemnable, regardless of the political parties or individuals affected. “We have observed the recent spate of violent attacks at political gatherings in parts of the country. The reported attacks in Edo, Cross River, and Gombe, and other violence targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines are condemnable,” the statement said. On the Lagos incident, the council said: “Our campaign strongly condemns the disruption of today’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos.” The APC-PCC urged political parties, politicians and their supporters to exercise restraint as campaign activities gathered momentum, warning against actions capable of creating public disorder. It called on security agencies to strengthen their response to political violence and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. “Political parties and candidates are enjoined to campaign on issues that uplift the lives of Nigerians and not to instigate violence at political events,” it added. Lagos APC denies involvement The Lagos State chapter of the APC also condemned the reported attack on NDC members in Ikeja but dismissed allegations linking the ruling party to the incident. The party’s State Publicity Secretary, Seye Oladejo, described the allegation as baseless, challenging the opposition party to present credible evidence to security agencies rather than make public insinuations. In a statement, Oladejo said the allegation was an attempt to drag the APC into an incident without credible evidence linking the party to the disruption. “We consider this allegation not only reckless, baseless and irresponsible but also a desperate attempt to drag Lagos APC into an incident for which the accusers have presented no credible evidence linking the ruling party,” he said. The party noted that the reported incident in Ikeja coincided with the official flag-off of its 2027 general election campaign in Epe, where its leadership, elected officials and stakeholders were mobilised. According to Oladejo, the APC could not have abandoned a major statewide political engagement to interfere with an opposition event. “For the avoidance of doubt, Lagos APC categorically rejects any insinuation of involvement, direct or indirect, in the alleged disruption of the said political gathering. We have neither sponsored, encouraged nor participated in any act capable of undermining the constitutional rights of any political party or group to assemble, deliberate and canvass for political support,” he said. Oladejo maintained that the APC’s position as the governing party in Lagos did not make it responsible for every breach of public order in the state. He described the accusation as “a lazy political reflex that substitutes propaganda for investigation and blame-shifting for accountability.” The APC spokesman urged the NDC to submit any credible evidence linking individuals or groups to the incident to the appropriate security agencies and allow the law to take its course. He also called on the Lagos State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) to investigate the incident and take measures to prevent any breakdown of law and order. Reiterating the party’s commitment to peaceful and issue-based campaigns, Oladejo said political ambition should not be used as a justification for lawlessness and urged political actors to avoid intimidation and disorder as the 2027 elections approach. items.title: Join Rainbow Coalition or leave, Fubara warns supporters
items.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has warned his supporters who are unwilling to align with the Rainbow Coalition to leave, insisting that his decision to return to his political camp is final. Fubara gave the warning on Thursday during the inauguration of the Rivers State All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Rainbow Coalition, in Port Harcourt. Addressing party members and supporters, the governor urged those whose names were not included in the campaign council list not to feel aggrieved, explaining that there were still sub-committees to be constituted and that the list could be updated. He, however, warned against double-dealing, insisting that those claiming to support him must demonstrate genuine commitment to the coalition. “We still have sub-committees. The list can also be updated so you don’t have any problems to worry about. The most important thing is to work with your heart sincerely. “Don’t openly say you’re with me and behold you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day. And anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way,” he said. Acknowledging that some of his supporters might find it difficult to accept the new political direction, Fubara urged them to put the past behind them and embrace the future. “Don’t go behind and say this is Fubara, no, no, no. I have said it. It might be difficult but we have gone past that. We are looking at the future and what God holds for us,” he added. The governor charged members of the campaign council to work together to achieve their political objectives, expressing confidence that the coalition would record more votes in the forthcoming elections than it secured in 2023. “Nothing is impossible. Provided it’s something that has to do with life, it is possible if we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023. “It is only for us to say yes, we want to do it. And I am very sure that with the strategy of these forthcoming elections we are going to come out with good results better than what we had before,” he said. Fubara also thanked the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, and other political leaders for their efforts in establishing the campaign council. Earlier, Wike, who inaugurated the council, announced plans to establish similar campaign structures across the 23 local government areas of Rivers State. He said the coalition would abandon conventional campaign rallies in favour of direct engagement with residents through community gatherings, family meetings and age-grade associations. “We are going away from that ceremonial campaign style. When we are going to Gokana today, we just stay in one field and begin to talk to those we already know. “It is going to be different. This time around we are going round to communities, to family meetings, to age-grade meetings and other informal sects to talk to them, not necessarily those we meet with every day. “You and I meet every day; then tomorrow again we gather in one place, we say we are holding a rally. We must depart from that,” Wike said. The minister commended Fubara for attending the inauguration and other engagements of the council despite his busy schedule. Wike, who is also the National Leader of the PDP/Rainbow Coalition, said members of the campaign council were selected based on their capacity to participate in its activities and deliver results. He urged them to mobilise support for APC and Rainbow Coalition candidates in the 2027 presidential, governorship, National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections. He further disclosed that local government campaign councils would soon be inaugurated to strengthen the coalition’s grassroots mobilisation. Background The development is the latest chapter in the prolonged political crisis between Fubara and Wike, who governed Rivers State from 2015 to 2023 and supported Fubara’s emergence as his successor. Their disagreement, which became public in October 2023, centred on control of the state’s political structures and influence over the Rivers State House of Assembly. The crisis split lawmakers into opposing camps and triggered repeated impeachment moves against Fubara. The dispute escalated in March 2025 when President Bola Tinubu declared a state of emergency in Rivers State, resulting in the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly for six months. The elected officials returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. Reconciliation efforts gathered momentum in 2026 after Wike announced an end to the feud and a reconciliation committee was constituted to engage Fubara and his supporters. The Rainbow Coalition, led by Wike, comprises political actors from different parties, including the APC and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), working towards Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. Fubara subsequently declared support for the coalition and endorsed Kingsley Chinda as his preferred successor in the 2027 Rivers governorship election. He also withdrew from the APC governorship contest, citing the need to promote peace and unity in the state. The post Join Rainbow Coalition or leave, Fubara warns supporters appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: De Miguel death made me thank God over Zidane headbutt — Materazzi
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Italy defender Marco Materazzi says the death of Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision made him reflect on the headbutt he suffered from Zinedine Zidane in the 2006 World Cup final. Materazzi said the incident, one of football’s most infamous World Cup moments, still troubled him 20 years later. He told Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport that De Miguel’s death made him grateful he had escaped serious injury. “The death of Jesus de Miguel made me thank God that nothing had happened to me,” Materazzi said in an interview published on Thursday. De Miguel, a Tenerife striker, died after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Segunda Division match earlier this month. Zidane, then captain of France, was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 final, which Italy won on penalties. Zidane, now France coach, said last month he was not proud of the headbutt but did not regret it. Materazzi said he and Zidane appeared to put the episode behind them when they met before a match in 2010, although Zidane later disputed Materazzi’s account of the encounter. “When he saw me, he hesitated a little, he even turned to walk back,” Materazzi said. “But I approached him and shook his hand: ‘I’m glad we’re meeting here, where nobody can see us.’ “He replied: ‘Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s all in the past.’ It’s a shame he later denied everything, saying he thought I was a fan.” France are scheduled to play Italy in the Nations League later on Thursday. The post De Miguel death made me thank God over Zidane headbutt — Materazzi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 3 terrorists killed, 2 civilians dead as attack on Mastung post repelled: state media
items.description: Security forces killed three terrorists on the N-25 highway in Balochistan’s Mastung district while repelling an attack on Kandawa Post, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing police. According to a spokesperson for Balochistan Police, terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan attempted a “cowardly attack at Kandawa Post on National Highway N-25 using an explosives-laden vehicle”. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. Security forces repulsed the attack through timely and effective action, the police statement said. However, two civilians lost their lives in the incident, while at least 13 others were injured, according to a list of names in the police statement. Three Frontier Corps personnel were also injured in the incident, the statement added. “The explosion caused damage to nearby houses and a mosque.” In the ensuing retaliatory operation, three terrorists were killed, the police said. The injured people were taken to medical centres for treatment. “The attack demonstrates that these terrorists have no connection with the people of Balochistan,” the police stressed. “Operations against elements seeking to undermine peace, development, and prosperity in Balochistan will continue, and the protection of the lives and property of the people will be ensured under all circumstances,” it affirmed. Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations. Earlier this month, a soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. In early October, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan in Mastung, Pakistan TV reported. Pakistan witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators during October , with terrorist attacks declining by 37 per cent compared with September, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). Balochistan recorded one of the most significant improvements, with terrorist attacks declining by 46pc, from 132 in September to 71 in October.

items.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms key to sustainable security, says Dare
items.description: Former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Sunday Dare, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms and social interventions constitute an important part of a sustainable national security strategy, arguing that insecurity cannot be tackled through military operations alone. Dare, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Thursday, said economic development, effective governance and social inclusion were critical to addressing the underlying conditions that fuel insecurity. He observed that public discussions on national security often focused largely on military interventions, while overlooking the structural impact of economic policies and social programmes on the factors that sustain insecurity. According to him, states with poor developmental indices often record high levels of fragility, reinforcing the need to complement military operations with investments in development and effective governance. Dare cited the security intervention in Birnin Gwari, Kaduna State, as an example of how improved security could support economic recovery and restore livelihoods. He said the intervention by Tinubu had enabled farmers to return to their farms, created employment opportunities for young people and improved productivity. He also credited Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, with providing an account of the development and its impact on communities in the area. Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s policies with security implications, Dare identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), local government autonomy and increased Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations to states and local governments. On NELFUND, he said expanding access to tertiary education would promote social inclusion and create opportunities for young people who might otherwise be excluded from educational advancement. According to him, providing legitimate pathways to education and economic opportunities could reduce the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgents and other violent groups. He described education not merely as a social investment but also as a long-term investment in national security. On local government autonomy, Dare said adequately resourced and accountable councils could strengthen government presence in communities through improved public services and development initiatives. He argued that responsive governance at the grassroots would reduce the opportunities for violent non-state actors to exploit poorly governed communities and public disaffection. The former minister also said improved FAAC allocations could enhance the capacity of state and local governments to invest in infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment and other essential services. He, however, stressed that such resources must be transparently and productively deployed to address socioeconomic grievances and vulnerabilities that contribute to insecurity. Dare maintained that security should be assessed not only by the government’s ability to confront threats through military force but also by its capacity to address the conditions that make insecurity possible. He noted that military operations remained necessary, particularly in confronting active armed groups, but argued that their gains would be more sustainable when supported by inclusive development, strong institutions and responsive governance. He urged Nigerians to broaden the national conversation on security performance by giving greater consideration to the developmental and social impact of government policies. The post Tinubu’s economic reforms key to sustainable security, says Dare appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria. Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency. He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another. “APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said. Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government. He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination. Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos. “Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said. He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices. “To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. We are together,” he added. The post 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pita : le corps sans vie d’un homme repêché dans la rivière Souma à Timbi-Madina
items.description: Le corps sans vie d’un homme de 36 ans, identifié comme Amadou Bah, a été découvert dans la rivière Souma, située entre les sous-préfectures de Timbi-Madina, dans la préfecture de Pita, et de Diari, dans la préfecture de Labé. Selon une source locale, la victime, qui souffrait de troubles mentaux depuis son enfance, était portée disparue depuis plusieurs jours avant cette découverte macabre. Joint au téléphone ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, le maire de la commune rurale de Timbi-Madina, Mamadou Lamine Diallo, est revenu sur les circonstances de la découverte du corps. « Hier, aux environs de 16 heures, les responsables de la jeunesse du district de Tiapata nous ont informés que des jeunes avaient découvert un corps sans vie dans la rivière située entre les sous-préfectures de Diari et de Timbi-Madina. Nous avons aussitôt alerté le sous-préfet, les services de sécurité et les agents de santé, avant de nous rendre sur les lieux. Des jeunes volontaires et des gendarmes ont ensuite plongé dans l'eau pour repêcher le corps. D'après nos constatations, la noyade remontait à plusieurs jours », a-t-il expliqué. Le maire précise qu'au moment de la découverte, l'identité du défunt n'était pas connue. Toutefois, un petit seau et des chaussures avaient été retrouvés sur la rive, du côté de Diari. Le corps a finalement été inhumé aux environs de 19 heures, tandis que des photos prises par les services de sécurité ont été diffusées afin de permettre à ses proches de l'identifier. C'est par la suite que les autorités locales ont été informées de la disparition d'un jeune homme souffrant de troubles mentaux dans le district de Tiapata. Les clichés ont alors été présentés à sa famille, qui a formellement reconnu le défunt. La victime, Amadou Bah, était âgée de 36 ans, célibataire et sans enfant. Elle souffrait de troubles mentaux depuis son enfance, a conclu Mamadou Lamine Diallo. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Pita : le corps sans vie d’un homme repêché dans la rivière Souma à Timbi-Madina est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Linguère : Mame Arona Bâ prend les commandes du commissariat
items.description: Le nouveau commissaire de police de Linguère, Mame Arona Bâ, a été officiellement installé dans ses fonctions, jeudi 12 novembre 2026, par le commissaire central de Louga, Ousmane Fall. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives, judiciaires, religieuses et coutumières, ainsi que des forces de défense et de sécurité. À cette occasion, Ousmane Fall a salué le travail accompli par le commissaire sortant, Ousmane Ndao, qui a dirigé le service pendant trois ans. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d'une collaboration étroite entre la Police nationale et les populations pour garantir la sécurité des personnes et des biens. Affecté au commissariat de Rebeuss, à Dakar, Ousmane Ndao a, pour sa part, exprimé sa confiance en son successeur, qu'il a présenté comme un professionnel expérimenté. Il a invité les populations à lui réserver le même accompagnement durant son mandat. Prenant la parole, Mame Arona Bâ a rendu hommage à son prédécesseur et sollicité la collaboration des autorités et des populations pour mener à bien sa mission. Abdoulaye Sadio (Correspondant)

items.title: Burkinabè contraints de quitter la Guinée: les acteurs nationaux et régionaux mobilisés autour des défis
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 12 novembre 2026) Face à la situation des compatriotes contraints de quitter la Guinée, la Présidente du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR), le Camarade Ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie KABORE, a convoqué une réunion de coordination avec les membres sectoriels du Conseil et les gouverneurs des dix-sept régions du Burkina Faso. Cette rencontre avait pour objectif de partager une situation actualisée de l'opération, de mettre l'ensemble des acteurs au même niveau d'information et d'examiner les dispositions nécessaires à sa poursuite dans les meilleures conditions. Composé de plusieurs départements et structures sectoriels au niveau national, le CONASUR s'appuie, au niveau régional, sur les Conseils régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR), placés sous la coordination des gouverneurs. Cette organisation constitue un levier essentiel pour assurer la cohérence des interventions, faciliter la remontée des informations et adapter les réponses aux réalités du terrain. La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré La réunion a permis de faire le point des actions déjà engagées par le Gouvernement. Depuis le déclenchement du dispositif interministériel de gestion de crise par le Premier ministre, le 3 novembre 2026, plusieurs mesures ont été mises en œuvre pour faciliter le retour des compatriotes et organiser leur prise en charge. Sur le plan logistique, 156 cars et 44 camions ont été mobilisés, avec l’organisation de cinq convois entre les zones de regroupement au Mali et le Burkina Faso. Au cours des échanges, les membres du CONASUR ont également été informés de l'ampleur de la situation. A la date de la réunion, plus de 43 800 compatriotes avaient regagné le territoire national. Ce chiffre témoigne de l'importance de la mobilisation engagée et de l'ampleur des responsabilités qui incombent désormais aux structures nationales et territoriales. Les discussions ont permis de mettre en évidence les principaux défis auxquels le dispositif doit apporter des réponses. Les préoccupations sanitaires et sécuritaires demeurent particulièrement importantes. Elles exigent une vigilance constante dans les lieux d'accueil et de transit, ainsi qu'une coordination étroite entre les services compétents. L'identification des personnes dépourvues de documents d'identité et le rétablissement des liens familiaux figurent également parmi les préoccupations à prendre en compte. L'accompagnement des jeunes majeurs, notamment leur retour dans les localités d'origine et leur réinsertion socio-professionnelle, constitue un enjeu majeur de cette opération. L'affinement du profilage doit permettre de mieux cerner les situations individuelles et de proposer des réponses adaptées aux besoins de chacun. Une attention particulière devra être accordée aux enfants en âge scolaire ainsi qu'à la prévention de nouveaux départs vers les sites d'orpaillage, dans des conditions précaires. À l'issue des échanges, le Camarade Ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité a donné plusieurs orientations aux acteurs nationaux et régionaux afin de renforcer l'efficacité de l'intervention. Elle a notamment instruit les gouverneurs de prendre les dispositions nécessaires pour assurer un accueil digne et sécurisé des compatriotes dans les localités concernées, tout en veillant à ce que ces derniers puissent exprimer leurs préoccupations dans un cadre approprié. Elle a également insisté sur la nécessité d'organiser des séances de sensibilisation à l'intention des personnes rapatriées, particulièrement des jeunes, afin de déconstruire les perceptions qui entourent l'orpaillage et de leur faire connaître les possibilités de réinsertion socio-professionnelle. Cette démarche vise à leur présenter des perspectives alternatives et à prévenir leur retour vers des activités d'orpaillage exercées dans des conditions de précarité et d'insécurité. La poursuite de la mobilisation des ressources et des appuis disponibles au niveau local a également été recommandée pour soutenir les différentes étapes de l'opération. Les acteurs sont invités à renforcer la concertation et à inscrire leurs interventions dans une dynamique de complémentarité. La collecte et la diffusion des données devront s'effectuer en relation avec les autorités centrales ou déconcentrées compétentes, afin de garantir la fiabilité des informations et d'éviter les initiatives isolées. La Présidente du CONASUR a, par ailleurs, appelé au maintien d'un dialogue permanent entre les différentes parties prenantes. Le partage régulier des informations, la coordination des interventions et la communication sur les mesures engagées par les pouvoirs publics doivent permettre de rassurer les populations et de préserver la cohérence de l'action collective jusqu'à l'achèvement de l'opération. Après le retour de nos compatriotes sur le territoire national, l’enjeu est désormais de garantir leur accompagnement et leur réintégration dans des conditions dignes et adaptées à leurs situations . La mobilisation des structures sectorielles, des gouverneurs et des CORESUR sera déterminante pour assurer la continuité de cette prise en charge et faire du retour au pays une véritable perspective de reconstruction et de réinsertion.
